items.title: Norris wins wet São Paulo race as Mercedes clinches the Constructors’ title
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Norris won the 71-lap wet-dry-wet race by 14.602 seconds over Verstappen, with Hadjar third. FIA Document 82 lists Mercedes on 652 points after Brazil; the result secured the team's ninth Constructors' title. The final classification places Lawson seventh after Leclerc received a five-second collision penalty.
items.why_it_matters: The title and race order are settled, not a pre-race scenario. Use the final FIA classification for points and positions after the post-race sanctions.

items.title: Mekies says Verstappen’s P21-to-P2 recovery exceeded Red Bull’s simulations
items.summary: Mekies said no simulation predicted Verstappen's recovery from 21st to second and that a small Friday issue forced the power-unit change behind the grid penalty. He also said McLaren was generally faster in the race. Verstappen described a markedly different balance after his strong opening Intermediate stint; Red Bull said it still needed to analyse the loss.
items.why_it_matters: Treat the drive as a standout recovery, not proof Red Bull had the fastest car or that a front-row start would have guaranteed victory; no race-time failure has been diagnosed.

items.title: Intermediates bracketed the soft-tyre phase as rain returned at Interlagos
items.summary: Pirelli reports all starters began on Intermediates and every driver used both Intermediates and Softs. Norris completed a 33-lap Soft stint, then 13 laps on a second set before returning to Intermediates as rain came back. Pirelli observed mainly thermal degradation with some graining on the drying surface.
items.why_it_matters: This is observed race use, not the pre-race set snapshot or forecast; the crossover and renewed rain reshaped the strategy.

sources.label: Pirelli’s official São Paulo race report

items.title: Vasseur says tyre temperature was central to Ferrari’s difficult São Paulo weekend
items.summary: Vasseur said Ferrari struggled to put both Intermediate and Soft tyres in the right temperature window; he estimated the effect could reach roughly half a second and said Hamilton's early slick switch may have been too aggressive. Leclerc finished eighth after a penalty, with Hamilton ninth.
items.why_it_matters: This is the team principal’s diagnosis, not an independent telemetry measurement or proof that one factor explains the whole result.

sources.label: Formula1.com on Vasseur and Ferrari’s tyre struggles

items.title: Stella credits cooler conditions for McLaren’s win and says more parts are planned for Las Vegas
items.summary: Stella said cooler-than-practice Sunday conditions helped McLaren control tyre temperatures and that the Interlagos updates worked as intended. He said additional parts are planned for Las Vegas as part of the 2027 foundation, without identifying components or quantifying their gains; he also noted continuing hot-condition long-run work.
items.why_it_matters: This is a team plan, not confirmation of an FIA filing or a measured upgrade effect. Las Vegas component coverage remains pending while FIA discovery is unavailable.

sources.label: Formula1.com on Stella and McLaren’s race
